easy.def: A big area of salty water.
examples: Fish live in the sea.
We swim in the sea.
The ship sails the sea.

more.def: A large body of salt water, sometimes another name for the ocean.
examples: We watched the waves roll in from the sea.
Sailors crossed the sea.
Fish and whales live in the sea.

easy.def: A tiny fish with a head like a horse.
examples: A seahorse swam by.
The seahorse held on to the plant.
We saw a seahorse at the aquarium.

more.def: A small fish with a head shaped like a horse that swims standing up and holds on to plants with its curled tail.
examples: A seahorse curled its tail around a blade of seagrass to stay in place.
The male seahorse carries the eggs until the babies are born.
Seahorses swim upright and move slowly through the shallow water.

easy.def: A sea animal that swims and eats fish.
examples: The seal swam in the cold water.
A seal clapped for the fish.
We saw a seal on the rocks.

more.def: A mammal with a smooth body and flippers that lives in the sea and catches fish.
examples: The seal slid off the rocks and dived into the waves.
A baby seal is called a pup.
Seals can hold their breath for a long time underwater.

easy.def: To close something tightly.
examples: Seal the box with tape.
Please seal the bag.
Mom sealed the jar.

more.def: To close something so tightly that nothing can get in or out.
examples: He sealed the envelope and put a stamp on it.
Sealing the lid keeps the soup from spilling.
We sealed the leftovers in a plastic box.

easy.def: To look for something.
examples: I search for my shoe.
We searched the house.
She searches the room.

more.def: To look carefully for something.
examples: We searched the whole house for the lost cat.
Divers searched the water for the old ship.
She searched her bag for her keys.

easy.def: The act of looking for something.
examples: The search took an hour.
We joined the search.
There was a search for the lost key.

more.def: A careful look to find something.
examples: The search for the lost kitten lasted all afternoon.
Scientists began a search for new planets.
The search ended when we found the key.

easy.def: One of the four parts of the year.
examples: Winter is the cold season.
What season is your birthday in?
Summer is the hot season.

more.def: One of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall, and winter.
examples: Fall is my favorite season because the leaves change color.
Soccer season starts in the spring.
Strawberries are in season in early summer.

related.def: The time before a sports season starts.

easy.def: A thing you sit on.
examples: Take a seat.
The bus has soft seats.
I found my seat.

more.def: A place where you can sit, such as a chair or bench.
examples: The movie theater has a thousand seats.
Please take your seat and open your book.
The back seat of the car was crowded.

easy.def: Coming after the first.
examples: I am in second grade.
She came in second place.
This is my second try.

more.def: Coming right after the first in order.
examples: The second runner crossed the line just after the first.
Turn to the second page of the book.
This is my second visit to the aquarium.

easy.def: A very short bit of time.
examples: Wait a second.
It took one second.
I will be back in a second.

more.def: A very short period of time, and one sixtieth of a minute.
examples: There are sixty seconds in a minute.
Wait a second while I tie my shoe.
The runner finished one second before her friend.

easy.def: Coming second in order or importance.
examples: The main road and a secondary road meet here.
Safety is more important than speed, which is secondary.
A secondary color is made by mixing two colors.

more.def: Not the most important; coming after the first or main one.
examples: The main road meets a secondary road at the bridge.
Green is a secondary color, made by mixing blue and yellow.
Winning is secondary to having fun with your team.

easy.def: Keeping something hidden from others.
examples: The plan was done in secrecy.
We worked in secrecy.
Secrecy was important.

more.def: The act of keeping something hidden or not telling others.
examples: We planned the party in secrecy so she would not know.
The club works in secrecy and has a secret handshake.
The surprise needed total secrecy.

easy.def: Something you do not tell other people.
examples: The gift is a secret.
Can you keep a secret?
I have a secret hiding spot.

more.def: Something that is kept hidden or known by only a few people.
examples: She kept the surprise party a secret for two weeks.
The recipe is a family secret.
He whispered the secret to his best friend.

easy.def: A person who helps with office work.
examples: The secretary answers the phone.
My aunt is a secretary.
The secretary typed.

more.def: A person whose job is to write letters, answer phones and keep records.
examples: The school secretary answered the phone.
My aunt works as a secretary.
The secretary kept the meeting notes.

easy.def: Without telling anyone.
examples: He secretly wished for a puppy.
She secretly hid a gift.
They secretly made a plan.

more.def: In a way that no one else knows about.
examples: The twins secretly planned a surprise for Mom.
She secretly hid the gift in the closet.
They secretly planned a party.

easy.def: One part of something.
examples: Cut the pie in sections.
The library has a kids' section.
This section is about frogs.

more.def: One of the parts that something is divided into.
examples: The library has a section for children.
Cut the orange into sections.
The paper has a sports section.

easy.def: Safe.
examples: The door is secure.
I feel secure.
The lock is secure.

more.def: Safe and not likely to be lost or harmed.
examples: The door is secure with two locks.
The baby felt secure in her mother's arms.
Make sure the ladder is secure.

easy.def: To make safe or tight.
examples: Secure the door.
She secured the boat.
He secures the load.

more.def: To make something safe, tight or firmly fastened.
examples: Secure the gate with a latch.
She secured the boat to the dock.
He secured the load with ropes.

easy.def: Being safe from harm.
examples: A good lock gives us security.
Hugs gave the child a feeling of security.
The fence is for security.

more.def: Safety from danger or harm.
examples: A seat belt gives you security in a car.
Locks and alarms add security to the house.
A warm hug gave the child a sense of security.

easy.def: People who guard a place.
examples: Security stood at the door.
Security checked our bags.
Call security if you are lost.

more.def: The people whose job is to keep a place safe.
examples: Airport security checked our bags.
Security guards watched the museum.
The concert had extra security.

easy.def: To use your eyes to look at something.
examples: I see a bird.
She saw a rainbow.
Can you see the moon?

more.def: To notice something with your eyes, or to understand something.
examples: From the top of the hill, we could see the whole town.
I see what you mean about the math problem.
He has never seen snow before.

easy.def: The tiny part of a plant that grows into a new plant.
examples: I planted a seed.
The seed grew.
A bean is a seed.

more.def: The small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
examples: I planted a sunflower seed in the garden.
Birds eat seeds from the feeder.
An apple has seeds in the middle.

easy.def: A very young plant that has grown from a seed.
examples: A seedling pushed up.
The seedling is small.
We planted a seedling.

more.def: A young plant that has just grown from a seed.
examples: A small seedling pushed up through the soil.
We planted a seedling by the fence.
Each seedling needs sun and water.

easy.def: To look for.
examples: We seek the treasure.
Seek help if you need it.
She sought shelter.

more.def: To look for something.
examples: The explorers sought the hidden treasure.
You should seek help if you are lost.
The animals sought shelter from the storm.

easy.def: To look or feel a certain way.
examples: You seem sad.
It seems cold.
He seemed happy.

more.def: To give the feeling of being a certain way, though it may not be true.
examples: The night seems quiet when it snows.
She seemed nervous before the big spelling bee.
The test did not seem hard to me.

easy.def: Keeping groups of people apart, which is not fair.
examples: Segregation kept people apart.
Segregation was against the law.
We learned about segregation.

more.def: The unfair practice of keeping groups of people apart, especially by race.
examples: Segregation kept Black and white children in separate schools.
Brave people worked to end segregation.
We learned about segregation in our history class.

easy.def: To grab.
examples: The cat seized the toy.
He seized the rope.
She seized the chance.

more.def: To take hold of something suddenly and firmly.
examples: The cat seized the toy mouse.
He seized the rope and pulled.
She seized the chance to speak.

easy.def: Not often.
examples: It seldom snows here.
I seldom eat candy.
My cat seldom comes inside.

more.def: Not very often; only now and then.
examples: It seldom rains in the desert, so plants there must save water.
My grandfather seldom travels far from his small town.
The shy owl was seldom seen during the day.

easy.def: To choose.
examples: Select a book.
I selected the red one.
She selected a card.

more.def: To pick something from a group.
examples: Select a book from the shelf.
I selected the red apple.
The coach selected five players.

easy.def: A group to choose from.
examples: The store has a big selection.
Pick a selection.
The selection of books.

more.def: A group of things from which you can choose, or the thing you choose.
examples: The store has a big selection of toys.
The library has a wide selection of books.
I made my selection from the menu.

easy.def: The person that you really are.
examples: She was her old self again after a nap.
Be your true self.
The kids were back to their usual selves.

more.def: A person as they truly are, or the way they usually act.
examples: After a good night's sleep, he felt like his old self again.
Just be your true self and do not pretend.
The twins were their usual selves, laughing and joking.

easy.def: Thinking only of yourself.
examples: It is selfish not to share.
The selfish cat took the whole bed.
Do not be selfish with the ball.

more.def: Caring only about yourself and not about other people.
examples: It was selfish of him to eat the whole cake without sharing.
A selfish player never passes the ball.
She realized it was selfish to keep the window seat every time.

easy.def: To give something and get money for it.
examples: We sell lemonade.
Mom sold her old bike.
The shop sells toys.

more.def: To give something to a person who pays you money for it.
examples: The bakery sells fresh bread every morning.
Our class sold cookies to raise money for the library.
He sold his old skateboard to a neighbor.

easy.def: A group of people who make laws.
examples: The senate met.
The senate voted.
A senator is in the senate.

more.def: A group of elected people who make laws for a country or state.
examples: The Senate voted on the new law.
Each state sends two people to the Senate.
The senate meets in the capital.

easy.def: A person who makes laws for a state or country.
examples: The senator gave a speech.
My state has two senators.
The senator met with voters.

more.def: A member of a group called the Senate, who helps make laws.
examples: The senator gave a speech about schools.
Each state in the United States has two senators.
The senator visited our class.

easy.def: To make something go to another place.
examples: I send a card.
She sent a letter.
Mom sends me to school.

more.def: To make something go to another place, or to tell someone to go.
examples: I will send a postcard to my grandmother from the beach.
The teacher sent a note home with each student.
The coach sent the players onto the field.

easy.def: Older, or higher in rank.
examples: My brother is a senior student.
The senior players helped the new ones.
She is a senior helper at the library.

more.def: Older in age or higher in rank or position than others.
examples: A senior pilot trained the new crew.
The senior class put on a play for the school.
He became a senior member of the team after ten years.

easy.def: A person who is older, or in the last year of school.
examples: My neighbor is a senior at the high school.
The seniors sat at the front.
Grandpa gets a discount as a senior.

more.def: A person in the final year of high school, or an older adult.
examples: The seniors led the parade on the last day of school.
A group of seniors goes walking at the park each morning.
Every senior wore a cap and gown at graduation.

easy.def: A feeling in your body.
examples: I felt a tingling sensation.
The sensation was cold.
The sensation of falling.

more.def: A feeling that you get through your body, such as heat or touch.
examples: I felt a tingling sensation in my toes.
The cold sensation made me shiver.
She felt the sensation of falling on the ride.

easy.def: Wonderful and very exciting.
examples: The show was sensational.
She gave a sensational performance.
We had a sensational day.

more.def: Extremely good or exciting.
examples: The magic show was sensational, and everyone clapped.
She gave a sensational performance in the school play.
We had a sensational view from the top of the tower.

easy.def: One of the ways your body tells you what is around you.
examples: Smell is a sense.
Dogs have a strong sense of smell.
Sight is one of your five senses.

more.def: One of the five powers of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching.
examples: Bats use their sense of hearing to find insects in the dark.
Your sense of taste works together with your sense of smell.
Humans have five senses.

easy.def: Good, careful thinking.
examples: It makes sense to wear boots in the snow.
She had the sense to ask for help.
That does not make sense to me.

more.def: Good judgment about what is wise to do.
examples: He had the sense to stay inside when the storm began.
It makes sense to save some of your money.
Her story did not make sense, so we asked more questions.

easy.def: To feel something without being told.
examples: I sense that you are upset.
The dog sensed that I was sad.
I sensed someone behind me.

more.def: To feel or become aware of something without seeing it or being told.
examples: Sharks can sense tiny movements in the water.
She sensed that her friend was upset.
Animals can sense when a storm is coming.

related.def: A tool that notices heat, light, or movement.

easy.def: Having good sense.
examples: She is a sensible girl.
It is sensible to wear a helmet.
A sensible plan.

more.def: Showing good sense and good judgment.
examples: It is sensible to wear a helmet when you ride.
She made a sensible choice.
The teacher gave sensible advice.

easy.def: Feeling things easily.
examples: My skin is sensitive.
She is a sensitive girl.
Sensitive ears hear small sounds.

more.def: Quick to feel or notice something, such as a touch, sound or feeling.
examples: The baby has sensitive skin that burns easily in the sun.
Bats have very sensitive hearing.
He is a sensitive boy who cries when others are sad.

easy.def: A group of words that tells a whole idea.
examples: Write a sentence about your dog.
Each sentence starts with a capital letter.
I read one sentence aloud.

more.def: A group of words that makes complete sense, starting with a capital letter and usually ending with a period or other mark.
examples: The teacher asked us to write a sentence using the new word.
A sentence has to have a subject and a verb.
He read the first sentence of the story slowly.

easy.def: A guard who stands watch at a gate or door.
examples: A sentry stood at the gate.
The sentry saw us.
The sentry kept watch.

more.def: A guard who stands in one place to keep watch and let people in or keep them out.
examples: A sentry stood at the gate of the old fort.
The sentry kept watch through the night.
The sentry asked us for a password before opening the door.

easy.def: To keep things apart.
examples: Separate the red from the blue.
She separated the eggs.
He separates the trash.

more.def: To keep or move things apart from each other.
examples: Separate the red marbles from the blue.
A fence separates the two yards.
She separated the egg yolks from the whites.

easy.def: Not together.
examples: We sat at separate tables.
They have separate rooms.
Separate bags.

more.def: Not joined; apart from each other.
examples: They sleep in separate rooms.
Pack the shoes in separate bags.
The twins have separate desks.

easy.def: Being apart.
examples: The separation was hard.
The separation lasted a week.
A separation of the twins.

more.def: A time when people or things are apart, or the act of dividing them.
examples: The separation from her friends was hard.
The fence kept a clear separation between the yards.
The separation of the egg yolk from the white takes care.

easy.def: The month after August.
examples: School starts in September.
Leaves begin to fall in September.
My sister was born in September.

more.def: The ninth month of the year, when autumn begins in the north.
examples: Autumn begins in September in the northern half of the world.
Apples are ready to pick in September.
The first day of fall comes in September.

easy.def: Things that come one after another in order.
examples: Put the pictures in sequence.
The sequence of numbers goes up.
The sequence is one, two, three.

more.def: A set of things that follow each other in a certain order.
examples: Put the story pictures in sequence.
The number sequence goes two, four, six, eight.
The sequence of events was clear.

easy.def: A leader of soldiers or police officers.
examples: The sergeant gave orders.
The sergeant saluted.
A sergeant leads a team.

more.def: An officer of middle rank in the army or police.
examples: The sergeant gave the order to march.
A police sergeant helped the lost boy.
The sergeant checked the soldiers' uniforms.

easy.def: A story told in parts.
examples: I read a serial.
The serial has ten parts.
The serial ends on Friday.

more.def: A story that is told in a number of parts, one at a time.
examples: The newspaper ran a serial about a detective.
The radio serial continued each week.
I watched the next part of the serial.

easy.def: A group of things that come one after another.
examples: We read a series of books.
A series of numbers is on the board.
The show is a series.

more.def: A number of similar things that come one after the other.
examples: The author wrote a series of books about a dragon.
A series of storms hit the coast.
The team won the series by winning four games.

easy.def: Not joking.
examples: Be serious, please.
She had a serious face.
This is a serious talk.

more.def: Not joking or silly; thinking carefully about something important.
examples: He had a serious look on his face when he told us the news.
Dad wanted to have a serious talk about the broken window.
The scientist was serious about protecting the rainforest.

easy.def: Very bad or very important.
examples: A big storm is serious.
This is a serious problem.
A bad cut is serious.

more.def: Important and needing careful thought, or bad enough to cause worry.
examples: A serious storm closed the roads for two days.
Forgetting to lock the gate is a serious problem for the farmer.
The doctor said the cut was not serious.

easy.def: In a serious way.
examples: I take it seriously.
She nodded seriously.
He was seriously hurt.

more.def: In a way that is earnest, or very much.
examples: I take my homework seriously.
She nodded seriously and listened.
He was seriously upset about the loss.

easy.def: A talk about religion or good behavior given at a church.
examples: The pastor gave a sermon.
The sermon was short.
We listened to the sermon.

more.def: A talk given at a religious service, usually about how to live a good life.
examples: The pastor gave a sermon about being kind.
The sermon lasted twenty minutes.
We listened to the sermon on Sunday morning.

easy.def: A liquid that is used in medicine.
examples: The nurse gave a serum.
Doctors use a serum.
The serum helps.

more.def: A liquid that is given as medicine to stop or treat an illness, or the clear part of blood.
examples: The nurse gave her a serum to help her fight the illness.
Doctors used a serum to treat the snake bite.
The lab tested the serum to make sure it was safe.

easy.def: A person who works in someone's home.
examples: The servant brought tea.
The king had many servants.
The servant cleaned the room.

more.def: A person who works in someone else's home, doing jobs for them.
examples: The servant brought tea to the queen.
In the story, the servants polished the silver.
The rich family had a cook and two servants.

easy.def: To give food to people.
examples: The waiter serves soup.
Mom served dinner.
We serve lemonade.

more.def: To bring food or drink to people at a meal.
examples: The waiter served our pancakes with syrup.
Dad serves dinner at six.
The cafe serves hot chocolate.

easy.def: To help people by doing a job.
examples: Firefighters serve the town.
The nurse serves the sick.
Soldiers serve their country.

more.def: To do work that helps a person, group or country.
examples: Firefighters serve the town day and night.
The library serves the whole neighborhood.
She served as president of the club.

easy.def: To hit a ball to start play.
examples: Serve the ball.
She served first.
He serves hard.

more.def: To hit the ball to start a point in a game such as tennis.
examples: It was her turn to serve.
He served the ball over the net.
Players take turns to serve.

easy.def: A person who brings food to your table.
examples: The server brought our food.
A server took our order.
The server was nice.

more.def: A person who takes orders and brings food at a restaurant.
examples: The server brought our pasta.
The server recommended the soup.
The server filled our water glasses.

easy.def: A computer that stores information for others.
examples: The server is down.
The website is on a server.
The server holds the files.

more.def: A computer that stores files and sends them to other computers in a network.
examples: The website is stored on a server.
The server is down, so the page will not load.
The school has a server for its files.

easy.def: Work you do to help people.
examples: The bus gives good service.
The shop gives fast service.
Mail service came late.

more.def: Work that is done to help other people, often as a business.
examples: The waiter gave us friendly service.
Bus service stops at midnight in our town.
The library offers a free service for borrowing books.

easy.def: A period of time spent doing one thing.
examples: We had a practice session.
The class is in session.
The first session was fun.

more.def: A period of time used for a particular activity.
examples: We had a long practice session on Saturday.
The art session lasted an hour.
The class is in session until three.

easy.def: To put something in a place.
examples: Set the cup down.
I set the table.
She set the box here.

more.def: To put something in a certain place or position, or to get it ready.
examples: Please set the vase on the shelf.
He set the alarm clock for seven.
We set the table before dinner.

easy.def: A group of things that go together.
examples: I have a set of blocks.
A set of crayons.
She has a tea set.

more.def: A group of things that belong together.
examples: I got a set of paints for my birthday.
The library has a whole set of books about space.
He keeps a set of tools in the garage.

easy.def: To make a home in a new place.
examples: Pioneers settled the land.
The family settled in a new town.
They settled by the river.

more.def: To make your home in a new place.
examples: The family settled in a small town near the sea.
Early farmers settled in the river valley.
They settled near the lake.

easy.def: To become calm or quiet.
examples: The dust settles.
Settle down, class.
The puppy settled in its bed.

more.def: To become calm, still or comfortable.
examples: The dust settled after the truck passed.
The puppy settled into its bed.
Please settle down so we can begin.

easy.def: A new town in a new place.
examples: The settlers built a settlement.
The settlement was small.
The old settlement is a museum.

more.def: A small community where people have come to live in a new place.
examples: The settlers built a settlement by the river.
The settlement had a few log houses.
The old settlement is now a museum.

easy.def: An agreement that ends an argument.
examples: They reached a settlement.
The settlement was fair.
The two sides made a settlement.

more.def: An agreement that ends a disagreement between people.
examples: The two neighbors reached a settlement.
The settlement was fair to both sides.
A settlement ended the long argument.

easy.def: The way things are arranged.
examples: The setup of the room is nice.
The new setup is clear.
The game setup is easy.

more.def: The way something is put together or arranged.
examples: The setup of the classroom is new this year.
The camera setup took ten minutes.
The game has a simple setup.

easy.def: The number after six.
examples: I have seven crayons.
There are seven days in a week.
My sister is seven.

more.def: The number 7, which comes after six and before eight.
examples: A week has seven days.
Seven kids played on the swings.
The bus arrives at seven in the morning.

easy.def: One more than sixteen.
examples: Seventeen kids are in my class.
My cousin is seventeen.
I counted seventeen stars.

more.def: The number 17, which comes after sixteen and before eighteen.
examples: My neighbor will be seventeen on her next birthday.
The team scored seventeen points in the first half.
Seventeen cars waited at the red light.

easy.def: Number seven in a line.
examples: I am seventh in line.
The seventh day is Sunday.
She finished seventh.

more.def: Coming after the sixth one and before the eighth one.
examples: He came in seventh in the race.
My cousin is in seventh grade.
The seventh chapter is the best.

easy.def: Seven tens.
examples: Grandpa is seventy years old.
There are seventy books on the shelf.
Count to seventy.

more.def: The number 70, which is seven tens.
examples: The old oak tree is over seventy feet tall.
A turtle can live to be more than seventy years old.
The bus held seventy passengers.

easy.def: To cut something right off or apart.
examples: A storm can sever a wire.
He severed the rope.
The tree branch severed the cable.

more.def: To cut through something completely, so that it is in two parts.
examples: The falling branch severed the power line during the storm.
Workers severed the rope to let the big flag drop.
The two countries severed their old trade link and stopped sending goods.

easy.def: More than two, but not many.
examples: I have several books.
She ate several grapes.
Several kids came.

more.def: More than two, but not a lot.
examples: I read several books this summer.
Several kids stayed after school.
She waited several minutes.

easy.def: Very bad or serious.
examples: The storm was severe.
A severe cold.
The pain was severe.

more.def: Very serious or harsh.
examples: A severe storm knocked out the power.
She had a severe cold.
The winter was severe, with deep snow.

easy.def: Very badly.
examples: The storm severely damaged the roof.
He was severely hurt.
The house was severely damaged.

more.def: In a very serious way, or harshly.
examples: The storm severely damaged the barn.
The plants were severely dry.
The teacher spoke severely.

easy.def: To join cloth with a needle and thread.
examples: I sew a button.
Grandma sews.
She sewed my torn shirt.

more.def: To make or fix things by pulling thread through cloth with a needle.
examples: Grandma sewed a button on my coat.
I learned to sew a pillow.
She sewed the rip in my pants.

easy.def: A big underground pipe that carries away dirty water.
examples: The sewer is underground.
Water goes down the sewer.
The sewer pipe is big.

more.def: An underground pipe that carries away waste water from buildings and streets.
examples: Rain flows into the sewer.
The sewer runs under the street.
Workers fixed the broken sewer.

easy.def: Making or fixing clothes with a needle and thread.
examples: I like sewing.
Sewing takes time.
Grandma loves sewing.

more.def: The art of joining cloth with a needle and thread.
examples: Grandma taught me sewing, and I made a pillow.
Sewing a button back on takes just a minute.
She has a sewing machine in her craft room.
